findings.title: Bind the executed skill donor to the approved donor root
findings.counterexample: Prepare/approve standalone adoption using donor A in the recipient project. Independently installed identical skill in project B has the same relative donor ID and byte-identical standalone receipt. Pass donor B to adopt_skill with the approved A plan. The execution comparison accepts ID/family/bytes, locks/validates/holds/retires B, and publishes recipient ownership of A resources. Donor A remains active and unheld. This produces two active owners in A and removes ownership in B without the grant having approved B.
findings.basis: Source-derived counterexample, not a runtime reproduction. TransferPlan has no donor-root field; the preparation root check is not repeated at execution. SkillDonor::hold validates relative resource/digest rows but no recipient root.
findings.correction: Retain and revalidate exact donor capability/root identity in the approved transfer through execution and recovery; reject substitution before any hold/retirement. Add one two-root identical-standalone-receipt negative fixture. Audit analogous deployment donor execution binding in the same correction.

findings.title: Address actual legacy deployment homes by their recorded project identity
findings.counterexample: An incumbent deployment uses DeployExecution.project="example" with target T and an otherwise representable owned file/OpenCode resource. Its DeploymentHome hashes "example", package and T. deployment_donor(T, package) instead hashes the GenericHost physical root correlation token; it looks in a different directory and returns missing donor receipt. No public argument can provide "example".
findings.basis: Source-derived functional failure, not reproduced. The legacy/OpenCode fixture starts with GenericHost::apply and rewrites only receipt resource spelling, so it leaves the physical-token home and cannot detect the mismatch.
findings.correction: Let the donor owner resolve/validate the exact existing logical project/package/target identity without moving or rewriting old receipts. Exercise a receipt produced by the incumbent deployment identity path, then import and restore through public donor APIs.

findings.title: Recheck the named explicit arena rather than its retained handle alone
findings.counterexample: Host A retains an explicit arena at /arena. Ordinary replacement moves that directory and creates a new /arena while destinations and their capabilities remain unchanged. A fresh participating host B receives /arena from the same configured coordination location. A compares its old held arena token to its old plan token; B compares the new held token to its new token. Both checks succeed and the wrappers acquire different lock files. A generic writer and nested-root coordinated skill writer can then enter the overlapping destination domain together.
findings.basis: Source-derived freshness gap, not a runtime reproduction or hostile-process claim. SafeFS documents root_correlation_token as held-root identity and explicitly requires reopen/compare to detect pathname replacement. GenericHost current_roots reopens project/user/settings but omits a separate explicit arena; both coordinated wrappers only compare the retained arena to itself. Deliberately choosing unrelated arenas remains outside the coordination contract; this finding is ordinary replacement of the configured common arena.
findings.correction: Apply existing supported current-name/root validation to the supplied arena before locking and recheck after acquisition, retaining its expected identity. Refuse the stale host before family/destination effects. One two-host ordinary replacement case suffices; no new lock primitive or security expansion.

notes: Scoped wrappers implement real existing writer calls; lack of upper CLI/MCP feature is not itself a finding because the accepted contract is host-library composition.

The named nested-roots test only checks two arena capabilities and manually creates an unrelated destination parent; it does not by itself prove two nested-root writer integrations. Existing standalone contention case exercises one actual writer.
